hub_subtitle: Business English para seguros, reuniões e entrevistas — e o desbloqueio da fala, do primeiro dia ao último

lesson.menu_title: Comparing Options -- Two Quotes, One Recommendation
lesson.menu_desc: A aula em que a Paula para de descrever e comeca a recomendar. Na aula 18 ela contou o que estava acontecendo quando o armazem 4 pegou fogo; hoje o cliente de Santos quer renovar e ha duas cotacoes na mesa: uma e mais barata, a outra e mais segura. A gramatica sao tres letras e uma palavra: adjetivo curto ganha -er (cheaper, safer, bigger) e a coisa comparada vem depois de than; adjetivo longo ganha more na frente (more expensive, more complete) — e nunca os dois juntos. Para apontar uma entre todas, entra o superlativo: the cheapest, the most complete. E so dois irregulares: good → better → the best e bad → worse → the worst. Seis palavras novas (cheap, safe, option, quote, coverage, discount), a folha de comparacao das duas propostas na tela, o Greg querendo a recomendacao numa frase, e a Sofia comparando voos e hoteis para Miami. -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 19 -- Comparing Options
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Paula Morales | Lesson 19 -- Comparing Options (Comparatives and Superlatives)
lesson.grammar_point: comparatives and superlatives -- -er + than for short adjectives (cheaper than, safer than, bigger than, busier than), more + adjective + than for long ones (more expensive than, more complete than), the + -est / the most for the superlative (the cheapest, the most complete), and the two irregulars good/better/the best and bad/worse/the worst

listenings.text: Hi, Paula. David here. Today I want to tell you about the worst recommendation I ever made, and it took me eight months to find out that it was bad. A client asked me for the cheapest quote. That was all he said: give me the cheapest one. So I sent him the cheapest one. I did not write a comment, I did not compare anything, I just sent the number. It was cheaper, and I was fast, and I was proud of that. Eight months later a truck with his goods was stolen on the road, and he called me. The cheap policy covered fire only. It did not cover transport. And he said something to me on the phone that I still hear today. He said: you knew, and you did not tell me. Now listen, because this is the whole lesson. Cheaper is a number. The spreadsheet says it, and anybody can read it. Better is a judgement, and the spreadsheet cannot make it. You can. And when you say it out loud, in one sentence, that is the moment you stop sending prices and start being a broker. See you soon.

Good morning, Paula. Sofia here, with the Miami trip in front of me. There are two flights on Thursday. The night flight is cheaper, nine hundred reais cheaper, and I know that looks good on the budget. But it arrives at two in the morning and your first meeting is at nine, so please think about that before you choose. The hotels are the same story. The cheaper one is forty minutes from the client's office. The other one is more expensive, but it is five minutes away, so your day is calmer and safer, and you arrive at the meeting fresh. Now the important part, and this is why I am calling. In November you will present the Santos renewal to the team in Miami. In English. Alone. I want the two options side by side, and I want your recommendation in one sentence at the end. Not a list of prices, Paula. A recommendation. And one more thing. In January you told me you were not ready to speak in a meeting. You were wrong then, and you are ready now. See you Thursday.

matching.title: Match each word to its meaning
defs: with no danger: nothing bad can happen there
the paper with the price the insurer offers
money off the price, so the client pays less
one of the things you can choose

items.situation: Greg asks: "Which quote costs less?" Answer with a full sentence, and say the two names.
tips: Option B is cheaper than Option A.
Option B is cheaper — fifty thousand reais cheaper.

items.situation: Explain, in one sentence, why the coverage in Option A is not the same as the coverage in Option B.
tips: The coverage in Option A is more complete: fire, flood and transport.
Option A covers more than Option B. Option B covers fire only.

items.situation: There are three policies on your desk and one costs less than all of them. Say it.
tips: This one is the cheapest of the three.
Of the three policies, this is the cheapest.

items.situation: The client says: "Just give me the cheapest one." Agree with the fact, then defend Option A with one reason.
tips: Yes, Option B is cheaper, but Option A is safer for your operation.
You are right, it is cheaper. But the answer to a claim is faster in Option A: twenty-four hours.

items.situation: Compare the two discounts for the new alarm system. One is 12%, the other is 5%.
tips: The discount in Option A is bigger: twelve percent.
Option A has a bigger discount than Option B.

items.situation: Greg asks: "So what do you recommend?" Answer in one sentence, with a reason.
tips: I recommend Option A, because the coverage is more complete.
Option A. The cheapest option is not always the best one.

bank.label: Comparing two options / Comparar duas opcoes
items: Option B is cheaper than Option A.
The coverage in Option A is more complete.
The discount is bigger in the first quote.
The answer to a claim is faster: twenty-four hours.
This policy is the safest of the three.

bank.label: Making a recommendation / Recomendar
items: Which option is better for this client?
Yes, Option B is cheaper, but Option A is safer.
The cheapest option is not always the best one.
I recommend Option A, and this is why.
For this client, Option A is the best choice.
